note: From the 2026-08-16 register-first verify pass (STVK gpo_bot_t layer). 7 trees verified and delivered to data/research/vilnius-verified.json. Leads failed only the evidence bar, the count, or ran out of the pass's time window; blocked can never ship as they stand. Register source for all: data/registers/lithuania-stvk-gpo.json. Extended 2026-08-17 (verification pass, session-435fb395): 3 trees shipped to data/research/vilnius-verified.json (vln_008 Sapiegos Park Linden, vln_009 Kalnai Park Pine, vln_010 Amur Cork/Crimean Linden group of Bernardinai Garden). Four candidates newly BLOCKED (2 likely-dead register entries, 2 locked-company-grounds trees in Zverynas). Presidential Palace oaks and the Castle Park chestnut circle researched but left as leads on judgement calls (security screening; ensemble-vs-grove read) rather than shipped or blocked. Extended 2026-08-31 (verify pass): 1 tree shipped (vln_011, Philologists' Birch of Sarbievijaus Courtyard, second source found on flf.vu.lt). CORRECTION: 'The oldest linden' / 'Seniausia liepa' (register 0310505050028, 54.698341/25.30911) is NOT a new tree, it is a duplicate of the already-published vln_008 (Sapiegos Park Linden, 54.698333/25.309083, same tree per its own Lithuanian Wikipedia page 'Sapiegų parko liepa') -- removed from this list rather than left to mislead a future pass. Two Žvėrynas candidates checked: Žvėryno liepa moved to blocked (delisted 2016, deteriorated); Žvėryno pušis stays a lead (no second source found in two search attempts). A passcheck brief this pass also flagged two other 'unmined' register rows that turned out to be exact-coordinate duplicates of already-published trees: the Sereikiškės nine-trunked willow entry (= vln_005) and a second 'Kalnai park pine' register row (= vln_009). Worth checking whether the register-diff logic behind passcheck's brief is comparing rounded coordinates; both were flagged unmined despite being live. Extended 2026-08-31 (second verify pass this window): 2 trees shipped (vln_012 Lazdynai Linden, vln_013 Dvarčionys Oak), both flagged for thin sourcing (existence+species corroborated by a second independent source each, but no age/girth/address found). Two more researched and left as leads rather than shipped: Mickūnų ąžuolas and Žudiškių ąžuolas, both corroborated as real by a second source (vietoves.lt's own Vilniaus rajono savivaldybė natural-heritage catalogue, fetched directly) but both sit in Vilniaus rajono savivaldybė (Vilnius DISTRICT, not city) at 12.8km and 18km from centre with no verified public-transport time, so the day-trip boundary (~30 min) could not be confirmed either way; shipping either as in-town would risk the exact 'day-trip boundary' violation BRIEF_RESEARCH warns against. Two non-tree register rows also disposed of: 'Habitat of plant species listed in the Red Book' and 'Dendrological collection of miniature conifers by Juozas Leleika' (see blocked).

leads.name: Group of four oaks in Sereikiškės park
leads.why: Researched this pass: confirmed real and corroborated by two sources (register + the Bernardinų sodas Wikipedia article, which lists it by name among the park's 1996 municipal heritage designations, alongside the Amur-cork/Crimean-linden group that DID ship this pass as vln_010). Still no individual description, photo or exact within-park position found, so I could not judge whether four separate oaks read as one compact standing point or as scattered plantings; that is the one thing blocking it, not existence or access. Worth a ground check or a photo next pass.

leads.name: Castle park chestnut circle
leads.why: Researched this pass, has its own Wikipedia page (Kaštonų ratas Pilių parke): NOT a compact single specimen but 35 chestnut trees planted in two circles around the abandoned 'Rotonda' pavilion, spanning 16 ares (1600 sq m), on the southwest slope of Gediminas Hill. Reads more like a planted landscape feature than a single collectible point (closer to the blocked Vingis linden alley than to the shipped multi-trunk single trees), though it does have one obvious place to stand (the Rotonda). In 2015 the municipality planned to thin out aging/weakened trees for lacking sunlight, which also raises an individual-specimen alive-status question. Needs a judgement call with a photo in hand rather than a text-only read; leaving as a lead rather than blocking outright since the ensemble test is genuinely borderline.

leads.name: Presidential park oaks
leads.why: Researched this pass: nine individual oaks (Lithuanian 'devynių šimtamečių ąžuolų grupė' means nine oaks each roughly a century old, NOT one 900-year-old oak; the Wikipedia article's own history section is explicit, 'jame tebėra devyni senieji ąžuolai'). Real park, first documented 1387, on the eastern side of the Presidential Palace at the corner of Totorių and Liejyklos streets. Access is genuinely open to the public (confirmed via a second search: gates on Universiteto street or the security post at Totorių g. 28, seasonal hours, weekdays 18:00-21:00 and weekends/holidays 11:00-22:00 in the warm season) but EVERY visitor and their belongings is checked by security personnel, which matches BRIEF's own 'a guard who checks: no' example. Left as a lead rather than shipped or blocked: it is not a locked-out private site, but the security-screening question needs a session judgement call rather than a night-run default, and the entry would also need to pick one representative oak or treat the group as the collectible point.

leads.name: Mickūnų ąžuolas (Mickūnai oak)
leads.why: Researched this pass: existence corroborated by a second independent source (vietoves.lt's own Vilniaus rajono savivaldybė natural-heritage catalogue, fetched directly, lists it by name under Medžiai/Vilniaus rajono savivaldybė), but that source gives no age, girth, address or condition, matching the register's own bare entry. Mickūnai is a town in Vilnius DISTRICT municipality (not city), roughly 4km beyond the city boundary and ~12.8km from the register point to the city centre; it has its own railway station on the Vilnius-Ignalina-Turmantas line, so a day trip is plausible, but two attempts (a schedule search and a Moovit fetch that returned no content) could not confirm the door-to-door public transport time against the ~30 minute boundary. Left as a lead rather than shipped or blocked: worth a transit-time check before it could be presented honestly as reachable from Vilnius.

leads.name: Žudiškių ąžuolas (Zudiskes oak)

blocked.name: Zverynas six-trunked linden
blocked.reason: Access fails hard rule 10: stands in the courtyard of GIS-Centras (a state geoinformatics enterprise) at Sėlių g. 66, on the company's LOCKED territory. Its own Wikipedia article states it is inaccessible to the public on weekends and holidays because the site is locked, and was unmarked on the ground as of the last check (2014). Not somebody's home, but not a churchyard-style open gate either: a guarded/locked company site a visitor cannot enter without arranging access first.

blocked.name: Zverynas english oak
blocked.reason: Same address as the blocked Žvėrynas six-trunked linden above (Sėlių g. 66, GIS-Centras grounds); no separate access information found this pass, and given the shared address it is presumed to carry the same locked-company-grounds restriction until a source says otherwise. Distinctive clustered-branch ('glaustašakis') crown form, 100+ years old per one web summary, would otherwise be a strong candidate.

blocked.name: Žvėryno liepa (Žvėrynas linden, T. Narbuto g. 20)
blocked.reason: Likely dead/declined: its own Lithuanian Wikipedia page states it was 'išbraukta iš saugomų medžių sąrašo kaip prastos būklės, sunykusi' (removed from the protected trees list as being in poor condition, deteriorated) per 2016 state cadastre records, and as of July 2014 the site carried no informational sign. Also a private-property edge case even if alive: it stands on the boundary of a residential plot at T. Narbuto g. 20, described as leaning against the plot's fence, though visible from public streets (Gervių, Paribio). The health finding alone is enough to block per the dead-tree pattern already applied to Vilnius's other delisted entries (Šiltadaržio chestnut, Rose Alley ash); do not re-research without evidence of a living, re-listed tree.
